reason: Biome treats a let declaration as one unit: it reports once per declaration (ESLint once per variable, so let { a, b, c } = x gives 3 vs 1) and stays silent when any variable of the declaration is reassigned (ESLint's default destructuring: 'any' still reports the others, as in argparse's let [prog, ...] = ...); chokidar's case is Biome's documented inner-function caveat.
